subject: Add infra for multinode jobs + enable data mixer for finetuning (#218)
message:
Add infra for multinode jobs + enable data mixer for finetuning (#218)

Adding the ability to submit multinode jobs, plus connecting the data mixer to finetune.py.

After this is submitted and the image is rebuilt, you can run multinode experiments like this:

`python scripts/submit_finetune_job.py --default_beaker_config configs/beaker_configs/default_finetune_multinode.yaml --config configs/train_configs/sft/tulu3_8b_preview_mix_v3.1.yaml --cluster ai2/pluto-cirrascale --workspace ai2/tulu-3-dev --num_nodes 4`

This will launch a 4-node experiment on `ai2/pluto-cirrascale`, with the config defined in `configs/train_configs/sft/tulu3_8b_preview_mix_v3.1.yaml`. The config and `submit_finetune_job.py` will mostly take care of things for you, but you need to make sure the value for `gradient_accumulation_steps` is set to the value you want given your intended batch size and number of GPUs requested (8 * num_nodes). Also, in `default_finetune_multinode.yaml`, `WANDB_API_KEY` and `HF_TOKEN` must be set to your personal secret values; the values in the config are placeholders.

Additionally, this now supports mixing datasets on the fly. Inside of your SFT config, you can define a data mixture like so:

```
dataset_mixer:
    HuggingFaceH4/no_robots: 9500
    ai2-adapt-dev/metamath-qa-reformat: 100000
    ai2-adapt-dev/codefeedback-single-turn-reformat: 156526
```

This will take the requested number of instances from each dataset and create a training file before launching your finetuning job. This training file will also be saved to the beaker dataset created by your experiment, so you can inspect it later if you want. If you want to add a dataset that isn't in a supported format, you need to add a function here to handle it: https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/main/open_instruct/utils.py#L215.

* Fix vLLM logprobs N-1 mismatch by only appending EOS for empty responses

Root cause: We were unconditionally appending EOS token when finish_reason='stop',
but not appending corresponding logprob. This created len(response) = N+1 but
len(logprobs) = N mismatch.

Fix:
- Only append EOS for truly empty responses (the actual edge case)
- When we do append EOS, also append NaN to logprobs
- Normal responses ending with </answer> no longer get EOS appended
- vLLM returns N logprobs for N tokens, so no mismatch

Also added assertions to verify masks match correctly. Updated diagnostic logging
to treat length mismatches as errors rather than expected behavior.

* Fix process_from_queue hanging issue

The bug was that the prefetch task was interfering with asyncio.wait. When
asyncio.wait included the prefetch task with return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED, it
would return immediately when the prefetch task completed (which happens quickly

This caused process_from_queue to return 0 almost immediately thousands of times,
even though there were active generation tasks running.

The fix:
- Only wait for actual generation tasks in self.active_tasks
- Don't include the prefetch task in the wait list
- Remove the special handling for prefetch task in the done set
- Properly wait for the timeout period when there are active tasks

This ensures process_from_queue actually waits for generation to complete
instead of returning immediately.

a ThreadPoolExecutor worker thread instead of the event loop thread.

- Maintains correct CUDA context (runs in event loop thread)
- Blocks the event loop during weight updates (necessary for CUDA)
- Properly handles exceptions and return values via threading.Event

* Fix process_from_queue hanging issue

The bug was that the prefetch task was interfering with asyncio.wait. When
asyncio.wait included the prefetch task with return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED, it
would return immediately when the prefetch task completed (which happens quickly
when the batch is full), without waiting for actual generation tasks.

This caused process_from_queue to return 0 almost immediately thousands of times,
even though there were active generation tasks running.

The fix:
- Only wait for actual generation tasks in self.active_tasks
- Don't include the prefetch task in the wait list
- Remove the special handling for prefetch task in the done set
- Properly wait for the timeout period when there are active tasks

This ensures process_from_queue actually waits for generation to complete
instead of returning immediately.

- Created sync wrappers for init_process_group, update_weight, ready, etc.
- Engine thread runs continuously, ensuring background tasks get CPU time

This ensures the vLLM engine's background task runs properly without
event loop starvation, fixing the hanging issue after step 1.

a synchronous callback on the event loop thread. This:
- Maintains correct CUDA context (runs in event loop thread)
- Blocks the event loop during weight updates (necessary for CUDA)
- Properly handles exceptions and return values via threading.Event

subject: Centralize optional tool setup with `maybe_load_tools` in grpo_fast (#1305)
message:
Centralize optional tool setup with `maybe_load_tools` in grpo_fast (#1305)

* Refactor tool loading into `load_tools` helper in grpo_fast

### Motivation
- Remove duplicated tool setup code and centralize tool registration into a single helper.
- Make it clearer how tools are created and how their stop tokens are registered with generation logic.
- Prepare for easier extension of tool types and reuse of the tool-loading logic across functions.

### Description
- Add a new helper `load_tools(args: Args) -> dict[str, Any]` to `open_instruct/grpo_fast.py` that creates and registers tools based on `args.tools`.
- The helper supports `search` (creates `SearchTool`) and `code` (creates `PythonCodeTool`) and raises on unknown tool names.
- Each created tool is added to the returned `tool_objects` keyed by its `end_str`, and its `end_str` is appended to `args.stop_strings`.
- Replace the inline tool setup in `create_model_and_optimizer` with a call to `tool_objects = load_tools(args)`.

- GB10 Blackwell GPU (sm_121, compute capability 12.1)
- CUDA 13.0 (required for Blackwell - not backwards compatible)
- aarch64 / ARM64 architecture

## Changes

### pyproject.toml
- Add vLLM v0.13.0 cu130 wheel for aarch64 (pinned to specific URL)
- Add PyTorch cu130 index for aarch64
- Exclude flash-attn on aarch64 (SDPA is faster on Blackwell)

### open_instruct/utils.py

### open_instruct/model_utils.py
- Make attn_implementation configurable (flash_attention_2, sdpa, eager)
- Default to sdpa when not specified (works without flash-attn)

### open_instruct/grpo_fast.py
- Use configurable attn_implementation (default: sdpa)

### open_instruct/vllm_utils.py
- Auto-enable VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION on aarch64
- Workaround for vLLM v1 msgspec torch.dtype serialization bug

### docs/DGX_SPARK.md
- Full documentation for DGX Spark setup
- Known limitations and workarounds
- Build-from-source fallback instructions

## Testing
- SFT training verified working on DGX Spark
- GRPO training in progress (requires serialization workaround)

## Notes
- This is experimental support - ecosystem is still maturing
- vLLM wheel is pinned to specific URL (may need updating)
- See docs/DGX_SPARK.md for full details

This adds the ability for datasets to specify tool definitions and active tools
on a per-sample basis:

- `tools` column: Per-sample tool definitions for chat template (overrides
  global definitions when pass_tools_to_chat_template=True)
- `active_tools` column: List of tool names that can be executed for each
  sample. If None/missing, all configured tools are active.

* Simplify: derive active_tools from tools column instead of separate column

Remove the separate ACTIVE_TOOLS_COLUMN_KEY - now the active tools for each
sample are derived directly from the tool names in the 'tools' column.

If a sample has a 'tools' column, only those tools can be executed for that
sample. If there's no 'tools' column, all configured tools are active.

* Optimize validate_dataset_tools to access column directly

Access the tools column as a list instead of iterating sample by sample,
which avoids per-sample overhead for large datasets.

* Fix HuggingFace cache invalidation for per-sample tool filtering

The per-sample tool filtering in rlvr_tokenize_v3 was not taking effect
because HuggingFace datasets has its own internal .map() caching that is
separate from our LocalDatasetTransformationCache. When dataset.map() is
called, HF computes a fingerprint based on the function code and kwargs.
If these don't change, HF returns the cached result even if our local
cache was cleared.

This fix:
1. Adds DATASET_CACHE_VERSION = "v2" constant
2. Passes _cache_version in fn_kwargs to change HF's fingerprint when
   transformation logic changes
3. Adds **kwargs to all transform functions to accept the extra parameter
4. Updates compute_config_hash() to include DATASET_CACHE_VERSION for
   our local caching as well

Now when DATASET_CACHE_VERSION is incremented, both HuggingFace's internal
cache and our LocalDatasetTransformationCache will be invalidated.

Instead of passing _cache_version via fn_kwargs (which required adding

parameter to override the computed fingerprint with one that includes

With TP > 1, the Ray actor was requesting 0 GPUs (num_gpus=int(tp==1)),
so CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES was never set. All vLLM engines on the same node
would default to GPUs 0,1, causing memory conflicts. Fix by requesting
tensor_parallel_size GPUs per actor and using TP-sized placement group
bundles.

With tensor_parallel_size > 1, vLLM uses the "mp" backend where
EngineCore runs as a subprocess. The IPC-based health check can
take longer than 2s when EngineCore is busy, causing spurious

subject: Add documentation and warning for dataset_mixer_list format (#1434)
message:
Add documentation and warning for dataset_mixer_list format (#1434)

* Add documentation and warning for dataset_mixer_list format

The dataset mixer uses a non-obvious convention where:
- Float values (with decimal): proportion of dataset ("1.0" = 100%)
- Integer values (no decimal): absolute sample count ("1" = 1 sample)

This is a common source of errors when users write "1" expecting the full
dataset but get only 1 sample.

Changes:
- Add docstring to load_dataset_configs() explaining the format
- Add inline comment at the parsing line
- Add runtime warning when integer count <= 10 and dataset > 100 samples
- Add format documentation to tokenization script header

subject: Fix training hang when inflight_updates is disabled (#1454)
message:
Fix training hang when inflight_updates is disabled (#1454)

* Fix training hang when inflight_updates is disabled

When `inflight_updates` is off, the weight sync to vLLM engines is a
blocking operation. During this time, vLLM engines cannot respond to
other Ray remote calls, including the health check. This caused the
training loop to hang indefinitely at step N+1's health check while
step N's weight sync was still in progress.

Fix: Add a `weight_sync_done_event` that signals when weight sync
completes. The health check now waits for this event (with a 120s
timeout) before attempting to call vLLM engines.

Flow:
1. Step N ends -> weight sync triggered (clears done_event)
2. Weight sync completes -> sets done_event
3. Step N+1 starts -> health check waits for done_event
4. Health check proceeds once weight sync is complete

subject: RLVR: remove redundant dataset shuffle that causes prompt/ground-truth mismatch (#1484)
message:
RLVR: remove redundant dataset shuffle that causes prompt/ground-truth mismatch (#1484)

The shuffle in setup_datasets() desyncs the "index" column from positional
indices. Since HFDataLoader._reshard() already shuffles via torch.randperm on
each epoch, the setup_datasets shuffle is redundant and harmful:

1. dataset[result.index] in accumulate_inference_batches retrieves the wrong
   example, silently pairing prompts with incorrect ground truths/rewards.
2. exclude_index() excludes the wrong examples from future iterations.
3. Checkpoint state_dict persists these wrong exclusions.

This removes both the train and eval shuffles and adds a RuntimeError guard
in accumulate_inference_batches to catch any future index desync.

Related: #1483

message:
Wait for vLLM update_weight RPCs before unpausing actors in weight sync (#1480)

* fix: wait for vLLM update_weight RPCs before unpausing actors in weight sync

In some instances, should_stop was set to False before all vLLM engine update_weight
RPCs had completed. As a result:
- vLLM engine(s) never complete the update_weight tasks
- check_background_threads.remote() could not be processed
- Main thread blocked indefinitely in health_check_fn()

Fix: Wait for all engine.update_weight ObjectRefs (returned by broadcast_to_vllm)
to complete before calling set_should_stop(False). This guarantees vLLM engines
are idle before the health check runs check_background_threads.

subject: Fix ZeRO-2 discarding gradients during manual accumulation (#1498)
message:
Fix ZeRO-2 discarding gradients during manual accumulation (#1498)

* Fix ZeRO-2 discarding gradients during manual gradient accumulation

With gradient_accumulation_steps=1 in the DeepSpeed config, every
backward() call is treated as a gradient accumulation boundary.
In ZeRO-2 (stage_1_and_2.py), hitting the boundary resets the internal
gradient accumulator (all_grad_tensors = None), so only the last
backward's gradient survives — all previous micro-batches are discarded.

ZeRO-3 doesn't have this bug because it uses a separate micro_step_id
counter that only resets in step()/zero_grad(), correctly accumulating
across all backward calls.

Fix: use DeepSpeed's set_gradient_accumulation_boundary() API to
explicitly mark only the final backward before step() as the boundary.
This works with varying accumulation step counts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

DTensor view ops are incompatible with torch.compile/inductor, causing

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

is disabled (e.g. for TP compatibility), fall back to full activation
checkpointing instead of no checkpointing, to avoid OOM.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The original compile failure was DTensor view ops in the loss computation.

work since it only sees regular tensors in the loss path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Compute per-token logps on local TP shards to avoid OOM from full_tensor()

Adds calculate_per_token_logps() which handles both regular and DTensor
logits. For TP, computes log-probs on local sequence shards (Shard(1))
and all-gathers only the tiny per-token scalars instead of the full
(S, vocab) logits tensor. Both get_batch_logps and _get_batch_logps
now call this internally, giving a single codepath for all forward
functions (HF, OLMo-core, packing, non-packing, TP and non-TP).

* Fix concatenated_forward_olmo and separate_forward_olmo to compute logps from logits

The olmo functions were passing labels to the model and using output.loss
as per-token logps, but the olmo-core Transformer returns a scalar mean
loss by default. Fix by calling the model without labels (returns logits
directly) and computing per-token logps with calculate_per_token_logps,
matching the HF path.

* Revert olmo forward functions to labels= path and remove dead collator keys

Revert concatenated_forward_olmo and separate_forward_olmo to pass
labels to the model and use output.loss for per-token logps. This is
the TP-safe path through DPOLMHead. Remove unused combined input_ids
and attention_mask keys from DataCollatorForSeq2SeqDPO that caused
double-counting in get_num_tokens. Fix GPU tests to swap lm_head to
DPOLMHead so the model returns per-token logps when labels are passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix drop_last=True in cache dataloader dropping samples

The reference logprobs cache dataloader used drop_last=True, which
discards the last incomplete batch at the global shard level. This
caused missing indices when dataset size isn't divisible by the cache
batch size. Use drop_last=False since the cache must process every
example.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix multi-node DPO NCCL hang during reference logprobs caching with packing

With packing enabled, different ranks can get different numbers of batches
due to overflow handling in HFDataLoader. This causes ranks to desync on
FSDP/TP collectives inside forward_fn, leading to NCCL watchdog timeouts.

Fix by synchronizing batch counts across ranks after the main loop and
running dummy forward passes on ranks that finished early. Dummy results
are discarded since the subsequent all_reduce(MAX) correctly picks real
values over the -inf defaults.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix NCCL hang: pre-sync batch counts before forward passes in cache loop

The previous fix (post-loop dummy forward passes) deadlocked because ranks
that finished the loop early tried to all_reduce on default_pg while ranks
still in the loop needed those same peers for FSDP/TP collectives during
forward passes. Neither side could proceed.

The fix collects all batches into a list first, syncs the max batch count
across ranks via all_reduce (at a safe synchronization point before any
forward passes), then iterates with a known target count so all ranks do
exactly the same number of forward passes.

* Fix ref policy checkpoint save under DeepSpeed ZeRO-3

When saving a checkpoint with ZeRO-3 sharding and 16 GPUs, calling
state_dict() on rank 0 only returns that rank's local shard (~1/16 of
each parameter), producing a ~3MB file instead of the full ~14GB model.

training model has step-N weights, causing KL≈2 at the first logged step.

Fix by using GatheredParameters (the same pattern as save_model) to
assemble the full tensors on rank 0 before saving.
